subject: Consolidation: evaluation/labeling vendors — scope alignment & sample pass rates
messages:
From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Consolidation: initial ask + samples needed

Team —

We're moving to consolidate labeling and prompt-eval contractors for the next 12 months. Benches: quality, turnaround, SOC2 alignment, and predictable unit pricing. I spoke to Procurement and Legal — they want a short list (2 vendors) with:
- representative sample pass rates on 3 of our internal prompt-eval projects (intent detection, summarization, rerank)
- SOW with SLAs and change order process
- sample pricing for 50k tokens/month baseline and 250k/month spike

Can Neha and Dev coordinate to request the sample exports from current vendors? Priorities: 1) sample pass CSV (per-case pass/fail and comments), 2) sample SOW, 3) turnaround SLA on review cycles.

I attached the RFP outline in Drive (link below) and a quick template for the sample request email. Please respond with vendor list and ETA by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Procurement Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cLabelingRFP
From: sara@labelforge.com
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@labelforge.ai
Date: 2026-10-02T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consolidation: initial ask + samples needed

Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the note. Attached is a zipped export of three representative sample sets and our internal QA pass-rate CSV (LabelForge_sample_pass_rates.csv). Summary: overall pass 87% on intent detection, 82% on summarization, 90% on rerank. We include adjudication notes for edge cases and a per-annotator confidence score.

SOW and pricing are attached as SOW_Labeling_v1.pdf and Pricing_Comparison_20261006.xlsx. Highlights:
- 48-hour turnaround for first pass at baseline volumes, 24-hour for urgent spikes (with surge fees)
- SOC2 Type II (certificate and audit ref in SOW)
- Change-order addendum included (Section 4)

Open to a short call to walk the team through the CSV format and our adjudication process.

Best,
Sara Kim
Head of Ops, LabelForge
sara@labelforge.com
Attachment stubs: LabelForge_sample_pass_rates.csv, SOW_Labeling_v1.pdf, sample_export_bundle.zip
From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-03T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: LabelForge sample exports + SOW — quick read

Forwarding LabelForge materials. Quick take after a skim:
- CSV format is usable but uses different pass/fail thresholds than our eval harness (we need to normalize).
- Annotator confidence field is helpful; we should ask them to include adjudicator rationale for failed cases (not just comment).
- Pricing model looks slightly higher on surge tiers vs BrightTag. We should ask for blended price for steady-state and a cap on surge premiums.

Action items I propose:
1) Dev: create a small normalization script and run their CSV against our eval harness (ETA 48h).
2) Marcus: ask LabelForge for adjudicator rationale where pass=false for the 200-case sample (so Procurement/Legal can evaluate).
3) Lauren/Evelyn: prepare short note on preferred SLA language (turnaround and credits) we want in the SOW.

One quick question: should we run a dark-comparison (blind rescore) between vendors? That will add ~3 business days but gives a fair apples-to-apples.

-Neha

On Thu, Oct 2, 2026 at 11:22 AM Sara Kim <sara@labelforge.com> wrote:
> [LabelForge attachments]
From: dev.patel@redwood.com
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-04T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: LabelForge sample exports + SOW — quick read

Running normalization now. Early notes (50 cases processed):
- Formatting differences: LabelForge uses 'Y/N' and our harness expects 0/1. Minor but must be mapped.
- Several summarization failures are borderline; their adjudicator comments are terse. Need the rationale text for accurate adjudication-threshold mapping.
- Rerank results show strong relative ordering but lower absolute NDCG due to different gold set construction.

I recommend the dark-comparison between LabelForge and BrightTag. I'll prep the anonymized test (script + drive folder) and ping both vendors to upload to the same folder. ETA: 72 hours to run both vendors' 3-sample sets.

-Dev

Attachment stub: normalization_script_v1.py
From: contracts@brighttag.ai
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor consolidation — BrightTag baseline pricing and clarification

Hi Marcus & team —

Appreciate the consolidation heads-up. We reviewed the RFP outline and attached a concise pricing sheet and proposed SOW (see Pricing_Comparison_20261006.xlsx). A couple clarifications:
- Our surge window is defined as any weekday volume > 200% baseline for > 2 hours. Can we negotiate a 1.5x cap instead of 2x for surges?
- We can include adjudicator rationale but prefer to exclude free-form PII in comments — will redact where needed.
- We support a blind-vendor comparison; we recommend a 3-day window for both vendors to upload and 2 days for adjudication.

If acceptable, we'll return a redlined SOW by Monday.

Best,
BrightTag Contracts Team
contracts@brighttag.ai
From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: sara@labelforge.com, contracts@brighttag.ai
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-07T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consolidation: evaluation/labeling vendors — scope alignment & sample pass rates

Thanks everyone — good progress. Agreed next steps:
1) Dev will run the dark comparison on anonymized samples (Dev ETA: 2026-10-08T16:00:00-07:00).
2) Sara/BrightTag: please provide adjudicator rationale for failed cases for the 200-case sample by EOD Monday and confirm surge cap (LabelForge: confirm 1.5x cap or provide rationale for 2.0x).
3) Legal (cc'd Lauren) to circulate preferred SLA language; Marcus/Procurement will propose credit buckets for missed SLAs.
4) I'll schedule a 30-min calibration call for Thursday to review the dark-comparison results and choose preferred vendor for pilot.

If vendors can provide a consolidated one-page SOW summary and a one-line pull for surge pricing by Monday that would be great.

-Marcus
Director, Procurement Partnerships
Redwood Inference

References: HubSpot deal DL-2026-0193, Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cLabelingRFP
